questions.q: In the traffic-light system, what is the safest and most valuable way to use AI on health, legal and money topics?
options: Getting a diagnosis or legal strategy you can act on right away
Understanding terms and preparing better questions for a professional
Confirming whether a contract is fair and enforceable where you live
Getting reassurance before deciding whether to see a professional
questions.explain: Explaining terms, summarizing documents and preparing questions are green-light uses. Diagnosis, legal strategy and big money decisions are red: prepare with AI, then decide with a professional.

questions.q: You're about to sign a lease and one clause confuses you. Which question to your AI assistant best follows the lesson's advice?
options: "Should I sign this lease, yes or no?"
"Is this clause fair and enforceable everywhere?"
"Can you reassure me this clause is standard?"
"What does this clause mean, and what should I ask?"
questions.explain: Asking for a verdict like "Should I sign this?" is red, while asking what a clause means and what to ask is green. AI can help you spot what to ask, but it can't confirm a contract is fair or enforceable where you live.

questions.q: You want AI to help you prepare for a doctor's appointment. What should you do before pasting your notes?
options: Remove names, birth dates and record numbers, keeping only the details needed
Include your patient ID so the AI can match your notes to your records
Ask the AI to diagnose you first so you know what the doctor will say
Leave out where you live so the answer stays as general as possible
questions.explain: The lesson says to strip out identifying details such as names, dates of birth and medical record numbers; "a 45-year-old with type 2 diabetes" is all the AI needs. You should also include your location and ask it not to diagnose you.
